questions.question: Find the area of a right - angled triangle whose base is 12 cm and hypotenuse is 13 cm.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Base of the triangle = 12 cm

Hypotenuse of the triangle = 13 cm

**Concept used:**

Area of a right angle triangle = (1/2) × perpendicular × base

**Calculation:**

Let the perpendicular be 'x' cm.

x² + 12² = 13²

⇒ x2 + 144 = 169

⇒ x2 = 25

⇒ x = 5

So, the perpendicular of the right angle = 5 cm

Now,

Area of the triangle = (1/2) × 12 × 5 = 30 cm²

**∴ The area of the triangle is 30 cm²**.

questions.question: In 2021, Sam received an annual increment in his salary by 40% but due to the recession in 2022, the company started taking cost-cutting measures and his salary was reduced by 15%. What was the net change in his salary?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In 2021 salary increased by 40%

In 2022 salary decreased by 15%

**Calculation:**

Let the salary of Sam in 2020 be 100a

So, the salary of Sam in 2022 = 100a × 1.4 × 0.85 = 119a

So, increased salary = 119a - 100a = 19a

Percentage of increase in salary of Sam = (19a/100a) × 100 = 19

**∴ The net change in his salary is 19% increase.**

questions.question: A rod of 5 cm radius and 52 cm length is converted into a wire of 100 cm length of uniform thickness. The radius of the wire (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the rod = 5 cm

Lenght of the rod = 52 cm

Lenght of the wire = 100 cm

**Concept used:**

Volume of a cylinder = πr² × h

Here, r = radius, and h = height or length

**Calculation:**

Since both wire and rod are an example of cylinder, then

Volume of the rod = Volume of the wire,

Let the radius of the wire be 'x'

According to the question,

π × 5² × 52 = π × x² × 100

⇒ 52 = 4x2

⇒ x2 = 13

⇒ x = √13

So, the radius of the wire = √13 cm

**∴ The radius of the wire (in cm) is √13.**

questions.question: If (y² + (1)/(y²)) = 74 and y > 1, find the value of (y - (1)/(y)).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(y2 + (1)/(y²)) = 74

**Concept used:**

(a - (1)/(a))² = a² + (1)/(a²)-2

**Calculation:**

(y2 + (1)/(y²)) = 74

By subtracting 2 from both sides we get,

y2 + (1)/(y²) - 2 = 74 - 2

⇒ (y - (1)/(y))² = 72

⇒ (y - (1)/(y)) = 6sqrt{2}

**∴ The required answer is 6sqrt{2}**.

questions.question: If a sum of money at simple interest becomes 45 times in 110 years, then in how many years will that sum become 23 times?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount = 45P

Time = 110 years

**Formula used:**

SI = (PRT/100)

Amount = (PRT/100) + P

**Calculation:**

45P = (PR × 11/10) + P

⇒ 44P = (PR × 11/10)

⇒ R = 40%

According to the question,

Amount = 23P

So,

23P = (40PT/100) + P

⇒ 22P = (2PT/5)

⇒ T = 55 years

**∴ The sum will become 23 times is 55 years.**

questions.question: Two trains 320 m and 205 m in length are running towards each other on parallel lines. One train runs at the rate of 70 kmph and the other train runs at the rate of 56 kmph. Find the time they will take to cross each other (in seconds).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two trains 320 m and 205 m in length are running towards each other on parallel lines. 

Speed of the two trains are 70 kmph and 56 kmph, respectively

**Concept used:**

When two objects run in opposite directions then their relative speed = Sum of their speeds

**Calculation:**

Relative speed of the trains = 70 + 56 = 126 km/h

Relative speed of the train in m/s = 126 × (5/18) = 35 m/s

Required time taken to cover the distance = (320 + 205) ÷ 35 = 525 ÷ 35

⇒ 15 seconds

**∴ The time they will take to cross each other is 15 (in seconds).**

questions.question: A can complete a task in the same time in which B and C work together. If A and B could complete it jointly in 10 days and C alone in 50 days, then B could complete it independently in:
questions.solution:

A complete the work in the same time as B + C work together

A + B can complete a work = 10 days

C can alone complete a work = 50 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of (10, 50) = 50 units = Total Work

Efficiency of C = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of A + B = 5 unit/day

A 40 - litre mixture of milk and water contains milk and water in the ratio of 7 ∶ 3. How many litres of water should be added to the mixture so that the resulting mixture has 60% of water in it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial quantity of mixture = 40 litres

Initial ratio of milk to water = 7 : 3

**Calculation:**

Milk in mixture = (7/10) × 40 = 28 litres

Water in mixture = 40 – 28 = 12 litres

Let x liters of water be mixed to make water 60% of the mixture.

(12 + x) = (40 + x) × 0.6

⇒ 12 + x = 24 + 0.6x

⇒ 0.4x = 12

⇒ x = 30

∴ 30 litres of water should be added.

**∴ The required quantity of water to be added is 30 litres.**

questions.question: The compound interest accrued on a sum of Rs. 20,000 at the end of 2 years compounded annually is Rs. 2,050. Find the compound interest at the end of the 3rd year.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The compound interest accrued on a sum of Rs. 20,000 at the end of 2 years compounded annually is Rs. 2,050.

**Concept used:**

Amount = P(1+(r)/(100))^n

Here, p = principal, r = rate, and n = no. of years

**Calculation:**

Amount received after two years = 20,000 + 2,050 = 22,050

According to the question,

22,050 = 20,000(1+(r)/(100))²

⇒ (22,050)/(20,000) = (1+(r)/(100))²

⇒ (441)/(400) = (1+(r)/(100))²

⇒ ((21)/(20))² = (1+(r)/(100))²

⇒ (21)/(20) = 1+(r)/(100)

⇒ (21)/(20) = (100 + r)/(100)

⇒ 105 = 100 + r

⇒ r = 5

So, the rate of interest = 5%

Now,

A = 20,000(1+(5)/(100))³

⇒ A = 20,000((21)/(20))³

⇒ A = 23,152.5

So, the interest = 23,152.5 - 20,000 = 3,152.5

**∴ The compound interest at the end of the 3rd year is 3,152.5.**

questions.question: If Tan 15° = 2 - sqrt3, then the value of Tan 15° Cot 75° + Tan 75° Cot 15° is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given **tan 15° = 2 − √3**, then **cot 15° = 1/tan 15° = 2 + √3**.

Since **75° + 15° = 90°**, we have **cot 75° = tan 15°** and **tan 75° = cot 15°**.

Expression = **tan² 15° + cot² 15°**.

Using **a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab**, where **a+b = (2−√3) + (2+√3) = 4** and **ab = 1**.

Result = **4² − 2(1) = 16 − 2 = 14**.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** tan 15° = 2 − √3

**Formula Used:** tan(90° − θ) = cot θ | cot(90° − θ) = tan θ | (a − b)² + (a + b)² = 2(a² + b²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50c63666e609e35c2aecb16bb63f1d737b3b4aca742858fb6a6fa37f8411976.png] 

⇒ cot 15° = 1 / (2 − √3) × (2 + √3) / (2 + √3) = 2 + √3

⇒ cot 75° = cot(90° − 15°) = tan 15° = 2 − √3

⇒ tan 75° = tan(90° − 15°) = cot 15° = 2 + √3

⇒ Expression = (2 − √3)(2 − √3) + (2 + √3)(2 + √3)

⇒ Expression = (2 − √3)² + (2 + √3)²

⇒ Expression = (4 + 3 − 4√3) + (4 + 3 + 4√3)

⇒ Expression = 7 − 4√3 + 7 + 4√3 = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

For any angle θ, sin θ = cos(90° − θ), tan θ = cot(90° − θ), and sec θ = cosec(90° − θ).

Trigonometric Values of 15° and 75°

tan 15° = cot 75° = 2 − √3 and tan 75° = cot 15° = 2 + √3.

Algebraic Identity

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). In this case, 2(2² + (√3)²) = 2(4 + 3) = 14.</p

questions.question: Akash sold a motorcycle to Navin at a profit of 10%. Navin sold it to Vinay at a profit of 20%. Vinay sold it to Vishal at a loss of 5%. If Vishal paid Rs. 62,700 for the motorcycle, then what was the cost of the motorcycle (in Rs.) for Akash?
questions.solution:

Navin sold it to Vinay at a profit of 20%.

Vinay sold it to Vishal at a loss of 5%.

Vishal paid Rs. 62,700 for the motorcycle

questions.question: The perimeters of two similar triangles XYZ and PQR are respectively 62 cm and 42 cm. If PQ = 21 cm, find XY
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ΔXYZ ∼ ΔPQR 

Perimeter of ΔXYZ = 62 cm

Perimeter of ΔPQR = 42 cm

PQ = 21 cm

**Concept used: **

If ΔXYZ ~ ΔPQR 

then, Perimeter of (ΔXYZ/ΔPQR) = XY/PQ = YZ/QR = ZX/PR 

**Calculation: **

According to the question,

we have ΔXYZ ∼ ΔPQR 

Perimeter of (ΔXYZ/ΔPQR) = XY/PQ 

⇒ 62/42 = XY/21 

⇒ XY = (62 × 21)/42 

⇒ XY = 31

**∴ The length of XY is 31 cm.**

questions.question: If px + qy = 1 and qx + py = (2 p q)/(p²+q²), then (x² + y²) (p² + q²) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Here, there are 4 variables but only 2 equations.

So, lets put p = q = 1

px + qy = 1

⇒ 1.x + 1.y = 1

⇒ x + y = 1 ----(1)

qx + py = (2 p q)/(p²+q²)

⇒ 1.x + 1.y = (2× 1× 1)/(1²+1²)

⇒ x + y = 2/2

⇒ x + y = 1 ----(2)

Here, again 2 variables but only one equation,

So, put x = 1/2, then y = 1/2

i.e. p = 1, q = 1, x = 1/2, y = 1/2

Now,

(x2 + y2) (p2 + q2)

⇒ (1/2² + 1/2²)(12 + 12)

⇒ (1/4 + 1/4) (1 + 1)

⇒ 1/2 × 2 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

px + qy = 1

qx + py = (2pq)/(p²+q²)

**Formula Used:**

To find the value of (x² + y²) (p² + q²) , we use the formulas for solving simultaneous linear equations and properties of squares.

**Calculation:**

Multiplying the first equation by p and the second by q and adding them:

⇒ p(px + qy) + q(qx + py) = p × 1 + q × (2pq)/(p²+q²)

⇒ p²x + pqy + q²x + pqy = p + (2pq²)/(p²+q²)

⇒ (p² + q²)(x + y) = p + (2pq²)/(p²+q²)

Multiplying the first equation by q and the second by p and subtracting them:

⇒ q(px + qy) - p(qx + py) = q × 1 - p × (2pq)/(p²+q²)

⇒ qpx + q²y - pqx - p²y = q - (2p²q)/(p²+q²)

⇒ (q² - p²)(y - x) = q - (2p²q)/(p²+q²)

Squaring and adding the above results eliminates x + y and y - x, allowing us to solve for x² + y²:

 (x + y)² = x² + 2xy + y² 

 (y - x)² = y² - 2xy + x² 

 x² + y² = ((x + y)² + (y - x)²)/(2) 

Substituting back into our first results, we get:

 (x² + y²)(p² + q²) = (1)/(2)(((p + frac{2pq²)/(p²+q²)}{p² + q²})² + ((q - frac{2p²q)/(p²+q²)}{p² + q²})²) × (p² + q²) 

After simplifying, this leads to:

 (x² + y²)(p² + q²) = 1 

**The value of (x² + y²) (p² + q²) is 1.**

questions.question: The radii of two circles are 9 cm and 4 cm, the distance between their centres is 13 cm, then the length of the direct common tangent is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radii of two circles are 9 cm and 4 cm, the distance between their centres is 13 cm

**Concept used:**

Length of direct common tangent= √{(distance between centers)² −(difference of radii)²} ​

**Calculation:**

Length of direct common tangent = √{13² − (9 − 4)²}

⇒ √{(169 − 25)}

⇒ √144

⇒ 12 cm

**∴ The length of the direct common tangent is 12 cm.**

questions.question: If an electricity bill is paid before the due date, one gets a reduction of 13% on the amount of the bill. By paying the bill before the due date, Ravi got a reduction of Rs. 260.39. The amount of his electricity bill (in Rs.) was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ravi got a reduction of Rs. 260.39.

Discount percentage = 13

**Calculation:**

Let the electricity bill of Ravi be '100a'

100a × 13% = 260.39

⇒ 13a = 260.39

⇒ a = 20.03

⇒ 100a = 2003

So, the electricity bill of Ravi = Rs. 2,003

**∴ The amount of his electricity bill (in Rs.) was 2,003.**

questions.question: A salesman marks his goods 30% above the cost and gives a discount of 10% on them. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A salesman marks his goods 30% above the cost and gives a discount of 10% on them.

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the goods be 100x

So, the marked price of the goods = 100x × 1.3 = 130x

Selling price of the goods = 130x × 0.9 = 117x

So, profit = 117x - 100x = 17x

Profit % = (17x)/(100x) times 100 = 17

**∴ The required answer is 17% gain.**
